policy.maintenance: When one side changes, the active agent must update the counterpart in the same session. Hooks remind immediately and block one-sided commits unless the changed artifact is synchronized or this manifest records an explicit artifact-specific status or exemption.

hooks.name: block-destructive-command.sh
hooks.note: Codex registers this script directly; Claude inlines the same logic in pretooluse-bash.sh so its Bash matcher emits one decision. Change and test both implementations together. Decisions are allow or deny, never approval prompts; ALLOW_CLONE=1 is the narrow clone override. Codex normalizes supported shell-tool payloads with lib-codex-hook-json.sh. Operational details live in both hook READMEs.
hooks.equivalence: Identical apart from the payload-normalization preamble; Claude's live behaviour comes from the inlined copy in pretooluse-bash.sh, not from this file.

hooks.name: block-dirty-tree-rewrite.sh
hooks.note: Blocks filter-repo and filter-branch only when the resolved target has staged or unstaged tracked changes; untracked files are deliberately ignored. Resolution uses git -C, then the last applicable cd, then the hook cwd. Heredoc bodies are masked, and ALLOW_DIRTY_REWRITE=1 is the explicit override. Codex normalizes supported shell-tool payloads; the scripts are otherwise paired. Details live in both hook READMEs.
hooks.equivalence: Identical apart from the payload-normalization preamble documented above.

hooks.name: block-elpaca-rebuild-uncommitted.sh
hooks.note: paired for Bash emacsclient guard; Codex side normalizes string-wrapped tool_input via lib-codex-hook-json.sh

hooks.name: block-github-write-command.sh
hooks.note: paired GitHub write gate for shell commands; blocks git pushes and recognized mutating gh operations unless the target repo matches an exact OWNER/REPO entry or OWNER/* account wildcard in agents/github-write-allowlist.txt. Codex independently classifies literal nested functions.exec exec_command records and denies ambiguous records via the shared lib-codex-hook-json.sh parser; its directly registered entry blocks bootstrap failures with exit 2. Claude delegates through pretooluse-bash.sh, which already converts delegated failures into denials.

hooks.name: lib-elisp-diagnostics.py
hooks.note: Identical closed literal inspection-command classifier and pending-identity formatter for the live-verification gate. Inspection never clears pending evidence; unknown command shapes, mutations and arbitrary execution remain blocked. Assumes normal installed tool resolution, not a shell sandbox.

hooks.name: lib-public-url-scan.py
hooks.note: Identical verified-route registry and literal curl/wget URL-operand classifier. Unknown syntax retains conservative scanning; payloads and raw/decoded URL tails stay scanned. Emits sanitized field/rule labels; tested by tests/test_public_url_scan.py.

hooks.name: block-secret-leak.sh
hooks.note: Claude delegates Bash; Codex extracts functions.exec calls. Both deny credential tools, classify brokers with lib-op-policy.py and permit closed Python document edits. Codex permits those edits only in a complete literal wrapper; decoded commands and original secret values remain scanned. Only Codex accepts apply_patch: lib-codex-paths.sh scopes exceptions per destination and denies moves out of secret files. Claude native Write/Edit/NotebookEdit policy and both registrations are unchanged.

hooks.name: lib-op-policy.py
hooks.note: identical 1Password broker output classifier called by both block-secret-leak.sh copies; tests/test_op_policy.py asserts byte-identity and runs the shared case table against both copies.

hooks.name: block-unguarded-ahrefs-api.sh
hooks.note: paired raw Ahrefs API guards; the Codex side accepts Bash, exec_command, functions.exec, and functions.exec_command events. Allows the free subscription-info quota endpoint and the ahrefs-api-guard wrapper, and blocks paid api.ahrefs.com shell calls that have not checked the live workspace reserve

hooks.name: block-sensitive-read.sh
hooks.note: paired; Codex side gates Bash, exec_command, functions.exec, and functions.exec_command sensitive-path reads and includes a Read branch for future tool-name compatibility, with Codex deny decisions replacing Claude ask decisions

hooks.name: block-texi-edit.sh
hooks.note: paired for apply_patch/Edit/Write path guards

hooks.name: block-unregistered-launchagent.sh
hooks.note: Routes LaunchAgent changes through ~/repos/launchd, denying hand-installed plists in ~/Library/LaunchAgents and launchctl bootstrap/load/enable/submit and bootout/unload/disable/remove; the denial names bin/launchd-install.py. Read-only inspection stays allowed, as does anything routed through that installer. Heredoc bodies are masked so a quoted path is not read as an invocation. ALLOW_LAUNCHAGENT_CHANGE=1 is the narrow authorized-change override. Claude reads tool_input file_path and command; Codex uses lib-codex-paths.sh and codex_shell_command. Details in both hook READMEs.
hooks.equivalence: Identical apart from the payload-extraction preamble documented above.

hooks.name: block-walk-list-access.sh

hooks.name: block-long-pipeline-run-unchecked.sh

hooks.name: fire-and-forget.sh
hooks.note: Claude utility wrapping notify-emacs-* hooks so the CLI doesn't block on emacsclient. The Codex copy was never registered and was removed when the redundant Codex notify-emacs-hook.sh registrations were dropped in favor of codex-hook-wrapper.

hooks.name: lib-codex-hook-json.sh
hooks.note: Codex payload/functions.exec normalizer: preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs and rejects ambiguous fields, lone surrogates and NULs. A separate closed literal-wrapper grammar limits document-edit exemptions to one complete call with inert metadata. The secret guard checks extraction status and every context. Recovers workdir only from a unique parent call. Claude uses native payloads but sources the shared Git classifier for paired live trackers; unknown syntax stays conservative.

hooks.name: lib-codex-paths.sh
hooks.note: Codex apply_patch path extraction helper; uses lib-codex-hook-json.sh for object-or-string payload normalization, and includes native Write.content and Edit.new_string in secret scans. Secret scanning validates native patch framing, keeps all nonexempt file sections, and denies moves from exempt to ordinary destinations without reading source contents. Native Write/Edit exceptions remain scoped to their single destination. Claude has no apply_patch entrypoint and reads its native edit and notebook fields directly.

hooks.name: lib-elisp-evidence.sh
hooks.note: Identical helper that issues and atomically consumes one-time correlation receipts for Elisp test and live evidence. Receipts prevent accidental copying and replay but do not authenticate against another process running as the same user. Unconsumed evidence expires after one day through cleanup of only user-owned regular receipt and claim files; test and live-verification markers do not expire.

hooks.name: lib-heredoc.sh
hooks.note: Identical heredoc-aware masking helper for the secret-leak and sensitive-read guards: heredoc bodies fed to a known data sink are dropped from command-word scans; bodies fed to shells, interpreters, or pipelines stay in the scan.

hooks.name: lib-python-heredoc.py
hooks.note: Identical classifier for quoted Python stdin heredocs in secret-output guards. Exempts parsed Pass statements and a closed AST language for text/JSON document edits in one standalone, directly invoked heredoc. Every import, binding, statement and call is validated; unknown Python shapes retain conservative string scanning. Only classified bodies leave outer-shell lexical scanning. Original input remains available to other secret checks; outside shell text is preserved. Assumes normal interpreter/stdlib resolution, not a Python sandbox.

hooks.name: lib-inert-mentions.py
hooks.note: Identical projection used by both block-secret-leak.sh copies once a protected tool name (pbpaste, pass, security) appears in quoted-literal-masked command text: the name is masked only when it is a plain argument of a read-only text tool (grep, rg, wc, cat, ls, git log/show/...), so searches and listings are not denied as credential reads. Command words, shell/xargs/find/env arguments, =-joined values and git with -c or a writing subcommand are left for the fail-closed rules.

hooks.name: lib-op-policy.py
hooks.note: Identical 1Password broker output-policy helper for the secret-leak guards: classifies an op-automations/op-desktop invocation as allow or deny by whether its stdout can carry a credential; unmatched shapes are denied.

hooks.name: lib-repo-root.sh
hooks.note: Shared repo-root helper copied for hooks that need command-context git roots. The Codex copy additionally asks lib-codex-hook-json.sh for an exact unambiguous parent functions.exec workdir when a nested Bash event omits it; Claude receives its native command context directly.

hooks.name: lib-staged-files.sh
hooks.note: Shared staged-file helper copied for commit gates; Codex usage comment references lib-codex-hook-json.sh.

hooks.name: commit-file-selection.py

hooks.name: load-elisp-after-edit.sh
hooks.note: Runtime-specific apply_patch/Edit/Write path adapters share the bounded manual export behavior. Both emit PostToolUse hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName and additionalContext, including sanitized partial-failure counts; a bare message field is invalid. Export failures use visible context with exit 0 because JSON accompanying a nonzero exit is ignored. No hook registration change is needed for the export-boundary repair.

hooks.name: notify-emacs-notification.sh

hooks.name: pretooluse-bash.sh
hooks.note: Claude Bash PreToolUse dispatcher in ~/.claude/settings.json. Runs cheap guards in-process and delegates heavier git/filesystem checks, including GitHub writes, to standalone hooks. Bootstrap failures block with exit 2; delegated failures, malformed JSON, and interactive approvals deny. Rewrites replace only command in the full tool_input, preserving timeout/run_in_background. Codex registers shell hooks directly in codex/hooks.json; its security guards also block bootstrap failures, without a Bash rewrite or delegated-response aggregator.

hooks.name: cr-card-body-gate.sh

hooks.name: cr-issue-comment-freshness.sh

hooks.name: block-untrusted-execution.sh

Both use the mirrored static classifier for recognizable transient package execution, downloaded interpreter input, and designated untrusted staging. Guards allow or deny, never ask; unexpected failures block. New Codex definitions require native hook trust. This routing guard supplements the VM boundary and does not establish arbitrary-code or malicious-agent containment.

hooks.name: lib-untrusted-execution.py
hooks.note: Byte-identical static untrusted-execution classifier. Reuses the existing lib-op-policy.py quote-preserving tokenizer without invoking its credential policy or executing the proposed command. Coverage and limits live in both hook manuals; synthetic fixtures in tests/test_untrusted_execution_guard.py.

Codex Asana token resolves to pablo@epoch.ai

mcp_servers.note: Epoch's Asana MCP is project-local and must expose the same server to Claude Code and Codex with the Epoch Asana identity. The audit checks account identity via Asana /users/me and never compares or prints token values.

registrations.note: Tracked global Codex instruction counterpart. The live ~/.codex/AGENTS.md symlink points here because Codex does not apply project_doc_fallback_filenames to $CODEX_HOME.

Mutable live global settings; hook registrations are added in place. load-elisp-after-edit.sh is registered with timeout 150 (matching codex/hooks.json) because it waits up to 120 s for the Elpaca rebuild before reporting. Stop forwards turn-end state to Emacs, while session-learning capture belongs to the Emacs agent-before-exit path because Stop is not true process exit. Ahrefs and GitHub guard registration is documented in claude/hooks/README.org. The LaunchAgent registry guard is registered on both the shell and edit matchers so plist writes and launchctl verbs are both covered.

Tracked source of the auto-mode classifier configuration (environment and allow entries, each list starting with $defaults). Installed by claude/bin/apply-auto-mode, which also offers --check for drift; run by the user, since the classifier's Self-Modification rule blocks a session from widening its own permissions. Claude-only: Codex has no auto-mode classifier.

Global registrations live through ~/.codex/hooks.json, outside repo-root .codex to avoid double loading. Lifecycle hooks use codex-hook-wrapper and an explicit Emacs socket. Shell matchers cover Bash, exec_command, functions.exec and functions.exec_command; edit matchers are collapsed for trust review. Guards allow or deny, never ask. The LaunchAgent guard covers shell and edits. Untrusted-execution routing is appended at shell index 15, preserving existing trust keys; new definitions require native trust and reload. See codex/README.org and codex/hooks/README.org.

Shared deny-by-default allowlist for agent-initiated GitHub writes. Claude and Codex guards block git push and mutating gh operations unless the target repo matches an exact OWNER/REPO entry or OWNER/* account wildcard here. The benthamite/* entry permits repositories in Pablo's GitHub account; other entries should cover only repositories or accounts Pablo explicitly authorizes.

Codex-only trust, plugins, theme, MCP, accounts and models; gpt-6-astra is default, project-doc fallbacks are off, hooks are on. Preserve existing state when trusting exact source/key/current-hash definitions. Untrusted-execution trust is recorded for eight homes; loaded sessions need reload. bin/skill-prune replaces managed tables, scans default/active/configured homes, deduplicates histories and rejects missing evidence; disabled state is skills-disabled.json. bin/codex-config-prune removes dead records. Repo moves require rewritten trust keys. See codex/README.org.

Ensures the live ~/.codex/skills directory is a symlink to the tracked codex/skills tree because Codex discovers global skills from ~/.codex/skills/*/SKILL.md. Also installs local gitignored private-skill shims from the encrypted private manifest.

Creates local gitignored private-skill shims under the live skill roots from ai-config-sync.private.json, so explicit private $skill invocations resolve without tracking private names or bodies in the public repo.

Codex-only command allowlist rules, pruned 2026-07-29 to generic recurring commands only (git add/commit/push/restore, curl -L, ps, emacs batch, emacsclient --eval). One-off approvals, dead-PID kills, the AGENTS.md symlink rule, and the arbitrary-command CODEX_HOME env prefix were removed; do not re-add task-specific or PID-specific rules. There is no Claude counterpart; material policy changes should be recorded here.

Reads Google Drive's native sync-error panel through the accessibility API — the only way to reach it, since Drive exposes no file or API — and marks each reported name stale or live by resolving it against the Drive tree. Drive's list does not clear itself when the offending path disappears, so the raw count overstates the problem badly; the 2026-08-03 panel showed 200+ errors against 8 live offenders. Owned by the fix-drive-errors skill.
